mainTopic: The root of the קנס dispute, and whether brothers who support their sister get her earnings
overview: The amud opens by finishing a מחלוקת about a man who falsely denies under oath that he violated a girl. רבי שמעון says the father's claim is really for the קנס, which a man is exempt from if he admits it. רבנן say the father is really claiming בושת ופגם. רב פפא explains that each side has a different idea of what a plaintiff would naturally go after. Then רבי אבינא asks רב ששת whether brothers who support their orphaned sister from the estate get her earnings. רב ששת says they do and proves it from the widow, whose earnings go to the heirs. The גמרא rejects that proof, because a man wants extra comfort for his daughter more than for his widow. רב יוסף then challenges רב ששת from a משנה, and after some back and forth רבא reads the משנה as 'her earnings are like her found items,' so after the father dies they belong to her. רב rules the same way, and רב כהנא learns it from a פסוק. רבה challenges that source, and the discussion of injury payments continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What the father is really suing for
steps.stepSummary: This finishes רבי שמעון's reason: the claim is for the קנס, and someone who admits to a קנס is exempt, so his denial is not a denial of money. רבנן say the father is really claiming בושת ופגם.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one who admits to a fine is exempt. And רבנן hold: when the father sues, it is humiliation and degradation that he is suing for.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining רבי שמעון's position. Then it gives רבנן's view of what the father is really claiming in court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון the claim is about the קנס. A person who admits to a קנס does not have to pay it, so denying it under oath is not denying money he owes, and there is no קרבן. רבנן say the father's real claim is for בושת ופגם, which must be paid even if the man admits it, so a false oath about it is a real denial of money.

keyTerms.meaning: A fine set by the תורה, a fixed payment rather than repayment of an actual loss
Someone who admits on his own that he owes a fine is exempt from paying it
Payment for degradation, meaning the drop in her value

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree that a person who admits to a קנס is exempt. They only disagree about which payment the father's lawsuit is really about.

phrases.english: And one who admits to a fine is exempt.
And the Rabbis hold:
when he sues,
phrases.notes: "He" is the girl's father, who is bringing the case to court.

phrases.english: it is humiliation and degradation that he is suing for.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation of the מחלוקת from the previous part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון: the claim is for the קנס, and one who admits to a קנס is exempt. רבנן: the claim is for בושת ופגם.

steps.title: What is the root of the disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what basic idea causes רבי שמעון and רבנן to read the father's claim differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the underlying reason behind the two views. This short question sets up רב פפא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father could be suing for the קנס or for בושת ופגם. The גמרא wants to know why each side assumes the father is mainly after one payment and not the other.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree? A question asking for the root of a מחלוקת

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the two positions just stated.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What basic assumption leads each side to its view of the father's claim?

steps.title: רב פפא: two ways to guess what a person really wants
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that each side has a different picture of what a sensible plaintiff would choose to sue for.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: רבי שמעון holds that a person does not leave aside something fixed and sue for something not fixed. And רבנן hold that a person does not leave aside something that the defendant cannot escape by admitting, and sue for something that the defendant can escape by admitting.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question. Each side is guessing which payment the father would naturally care about most.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון says the father would choose the קנס because it is a fixed amount, while בושת ופגם have to be estimated by בית דין. רבנן say the father would choose בושת ופגם, because the man cannot get out of paying them by admitting, but he can get out of the קנס by admitting. So each side focuses on a different advantage.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון: people go after a fixed amount (the קנס). רבנן: people go after money the other side cannot escape by admitting (בושת ופגם).

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Rabbi Shimon holds:
a person does not leave aside something that is fixed
phrases.notes: "Something fixed" is the קנס, a set amount.

phrases.english: and sue for something that is not fixed.
And the Rabbis hold:
a person does not leave aside something
that, if the defendant admits to it, he is not exempt,
phrases.notes: This means בושת ופגם, which he must pay even after admitting.

phrases.english: and sue for something
that, if the defendant admits to it, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree about what a plaintiff naturally prefers: a fixed amount (רבי שמעון) or a payment that admitting cannot cancel (רבנן).

steps.title: Who gets the earnings of a daughter supported by her brothers?
steps.stepSummary: A new topic begins. רבי אבינא asks רב ששת who gets the earnings of an orphaned daughter whom her brothers support from the estate.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבינא asked רב ששת: a daughter who is supported by the brothers, to whom do her earnings belong?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new question. רבי אבינא asks whether the brothers who support their sister get her earnings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A father gets his daughter's earnings (מעשה ידיה). After the father dies, the כתובה condition requires her to be supported from his estate, which now belongs to the brothers. The question is whether the right to her earnings passes to the brothers too.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him, a formula for putting a question to a teacher
Who is supported, given food and support

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אֲבִינָא מֵרַב שֵׁשֶׁת:
phrases.english: Rabbi Avina asked Rav Sheshet:
a daughter who is supported by the brothers,
to whom do her earnings belong?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אֲבִינָא מֵרַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, separate from the קנס discussion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do the brothers who support their sister receive her earnings?

steps.title: First side: the brothers take the father's place
steps.stepSummary: One possibility is that the brothers stand in the father's place, so her earnings go to them just as they went to the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: They stand in place of the father. Just as there, her earnings go to the father, here too her earnings go to the brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבינא explains the first side of his question. Maybe the brothers count like the father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the brothers now carry out the father's duty to support her, maybe they also take over his right to her earnings. This side compares the brothers directly to a living father.

keyTerms.meaning: They stand in the father's place
Just as there, so too here: a formula for comparing cases

phrases.english: They stand in place of the father;
just as there,
phrases.notes: "There" is when the father is alive.

phrases.english: her earnings go to the father,
here too,
her earnings go to the brothers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Lays out the first side of רבי אבינא's question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do the brothers count as the father regarding her earnings?

steps.title: Second side: the brothers are not like the father
steps.stepSummary: The other possibility is that the brothers are different. The father supported her from his own money, but the brothers support her from their father's estate, not from their own money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps it is not like a father. There, she is supported from his own property; here, she is not supported from theirs.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבינא gives the other side of his question. Maybe the brothers do not get her earnings at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A father gets her earnings because he supports her with his own money. The brothers only pay her support out of the father's estate, as the כתובה requires, so it is not really their own money. Without that reason, they may have no claim to her earnings. רב ששת answers the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps: introduces the other side of a question

steps.confusionAlert: The brothers do pay for her support. The point is that the support legally comes from the father's estate, not from the brothers' own money.

phrases.english: Or perhaps it is not similar to a father.
There, she is supported from his own property,
here, she is not supported from theirs.
phrases.notes: Her support comes from what their father left, which he obligated through the כתובה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite side of the question, pushing back on the comparison in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the fact that her support comes from the estate, not from the brothers' own money, take away their right to her earnings?

steps.title: רב ששת brings a proof from the widow
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers from a משנה: a widow is fed from the orphans' property, yet her earnings belong to them. The same should be true for a daughter fed by her brothers.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You already learned this. A widow is fed from the orphans' property, and her earnings belong to them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers רבי אבינא's question by pointing to a משנה about a widow. If the heirs get the widow's earnings, they should also get the daughter's earnings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A widow, like the daughter, is fed from the dead man's estate and not from the heirs' own money. Even so, the heirs keep her earnings. So the fact that the brothers feed the daughter from the father's money, which was the worry in step 6, should not stop them from getting her earnings either.

keyTerms.meaning: You have already learned it (in a משנה)
Her earnings, literally 'the work of her hands'
Orphans; here, the dead man's heirs

phrases.english: He said to him: You learned it already:
phrases.notes: רב ששת is answering רבי אבינא. He points to a משנה found later in כתובות.

phrases.english: A widow is fed from the property of the orphans
and her earnings are theirs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in steps 4 to 6 with a proof from a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That the brothers get the earnings of the daughter they support from the estate.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: a widow is fed from the orphans' property, and her earnings are theirs.

steps.title: A widow and a daughter are not the same
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. A man does not especially want his widow to have extra comfort, but he does want that for his daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are these cases really the same? With his widow, he does not care for her to have extra comfort. With his daughter, he does want her to have extra comfort.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב ששת's proof. It says the widow case cannot teach us about the daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We think about what the dead man would have wanted. For his widow, he only wanted her to get her basic support, so her earnings go to the heirs. For his daughter, he would want her to keep her earnings and have something extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Are they comparable? A phrase that rejects a comparison
He is pleased with it / it suits him
Extra comfort, more than the basic minimum

phrases.english: Are they comparable?
His widow: he is not pleased for her to have extra comfort.
phrases.notes: 'He' means the man who died, the husband and father.

phrases.english: His daughter: he is pleased for her to have extra comfort.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from the widow brought in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between widow and daughter, so the question is left unresolved by this proof.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The father's wishes are different. He wants his daughter to have extra comfort, but he does not feel that way about his widow.

steps.title: But a widow comes before a daughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that a man favors his daughter over his widow. רבי אבא in the name of רבי יוסי teaches that when the estate is small, the widow is fed and the daughter must go begging.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does that mean his daughter matters more to him than his widow? But רבי אבא said in the name of רבי יוסי: חכמים treated a widow compared to a daughter the way they treated a daughter compared to brothers when the estate is small. Just as the daughter is fed and the brothers go begging at doors, so too the widow is fed and the daughter goes begging at doors.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 8. A teaching of רבי יוסי seems to show that the widow is put ahead of the daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the estate is too small to feed everyone, the daughter is fed before her brothers. In the same way, the widow is fed before the daughter. That ranking suggests the man cares more for his widow, which goes against what step 8 said.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? It introduces a surprising conclusion that will be challenged
Is preferred by him / matters more to him
A small estate, not enough to support everyone

phrases.english: Is that to say that his daughter is preferred by him over his widow?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Abba say that Rabbi Yosei said:
They made a widow, compared with the daughter,
like the daughter compared with the brothers, in a small estate,
phrases.notes: A small estate here means there is not enough money to feed everyone.

phrases.english: just as with a daughter compared with the brothers,

phrases.aramaic: הַבַּת נִיזּוֹנֶת, וְהָאַחִין יִשְׁאֲלוּ עַל הַפְּתָחִים,
phrases.english: the daughter is fed, and the brothers must beg at the doors,
so too with a widow compared with the daughter:

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָנָה נִיזּוֹנֶת, וְהַבַּת תִּשְׁאַל עַל הַפְּתָחִים.
phrases.english: the widow is fed, and the daughter must beg at the doors.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּבִתּוֹ עֲדִיפָא לֵיהּ מֵאַלְמְנָתוֹ? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of step 8, that a man prefers his daughter.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 8 that a man wants comfort for his daughter more than for his widow.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוסי ranks the widow ahead of the daughter when the estate is small. That shows the widow matters more to the man.

steps.title: Shame versus comfort
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that there are two different concerns. To spare someone from shame, the man puts his widow first. For extra comfort, he puts his daughter first.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it comes to shame, his widow matters more to him. When it comes to extra comfort, his daughter matters more to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by splitting the man's wishes into two areas, so both teachings can be true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's rule is about someone having to beg, which is shameful. A man would rather his daughter suffer that than his widow. Step 8 was about extra comfort beyond the basics, and there the daughter comes first.

keyTerms.meaning: With regard to / when it comes to

steps.whatToRemember: A man's wishes are split in two. To spare someone from shame, the widow comes first. For extra comfort, the daughter comes first. So step 8's rejection of רב ששת's proof still stands.

phrases.english: With regard to shame, his widow is preferred by him.
phrases.notes: Having to beg at doors is the shame. He would rather spare his widow from it.

phrases.english: With regard to extra comfort, his daughter is preferred by him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9 and defends step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the concern into two areas: avoiding shame versus giving extra comfort.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the widow is fed before the daughter, the man must care more for his widow in every way.
steps.terutzMaskana: He cares more about sparing his widow from shame, but more about giving his daughter extra comfort. So the widow case cannot prove who gets the daughter's earnings.

steps.title: רב יוסף objects from a משנה about the daughter's earnings
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף quotes a משנה saying a daughter's earnings from her father's lifetime go to the brothers. He infers that her earnings after his death are her own, even when she is fed from the estate. That contradicts רב ששת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objected: The משנה says that a daughter's earnings and the things she found, even if she hasn't collected them yet, belong to the brothers once the father dies. The reason is that she earned them while the father was alive. So what she earns after the father's death must be hers. Isn't the משנה talking even about a daughter who is fed from the estate?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a משנה to challenge רב ששת's ruling that a fed daughter's earnings go to her brothers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only gives the brothers what she earned while the father was alive. רב יוסף reads it closely: that implies anything she earns after his death is hers. If this applies even to a daughter being fed from the estate, then רב ששת is wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection from a source
She is fed (supported) from the estate

phrases.english: Rav Yosef raised an objection:
Her earnings and the things she found,
even though she has not collected them,

phrases.aramaic: מֵת הָאָב הֲרֵי הֵן שֶׁל אַחִין.
phrases.english: if the father died, they belong to the brothers.
The reason is that this was in the father's lifetime,
which means that after the father's death
her earnings are her own.
Isn't it talking even about a daughter who is fed from the estate?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge against רב ששת's ruling, after the side discussion about widow versus daughter is settled.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's ruling that a daughter fed by the brothers gives them her earnings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה implies that earnings after the father's death belong to her, and it seems to include a daughter who is fed.

steps.title: The משנה speaks of a daughter who is not fed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה's implication applies only to a daughter who is not being fed from the estate.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The משנה is talking about a daughter who is not being fed from the estate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב ששת by limiting the משנה to a daughter who supports herself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the brothers do not feed her, it makes sense that she keeps what she earns. That leaves רב ששת's ruling about a daughter who is fed untouched.

keyTerms.meaning: A daughter who is not fed from the estate

phrases.english: No, it is talking about a daughter who is not fed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's objection by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's implication covers even a daughter who is fed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The implication only covers a daughter who is not fed.

steps.title: If she is not fed, the משנה would be stating the obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the answer. Some hold that a master need not feed a Canaanite slave who works for him. Even by that view, a Hebrew slave must be fed if he works, so a daughter surely keeps her earnings if nobody feeds her. Why would the משנה need to teach that?
steps.simpleTranslation: If she is not fed, why say it at all? Some hold that a master may tell his slave 'Work for me, but I won't feed you.' Even according to them, that is only for an עבד כנעני, since the תורה does not write 'with you' about him. But for an עבד עברי, about whom the תורה writes 'with you,' the master may not do this. All the more so for the father's daughter!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave: if the daughter isn't fed, it's too obvious that she keeps her earnings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה says an עבד עברי lives 'with you,' so his master cannot make him work without feeding him. A daughter deserves at least as much as an עבד עברי. So the brothers obviously cannot take her earnings without feeding her, and the משנה would be teaching nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: 'With you,' the Torah's phrase about the Hebrew slave

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not asking whether a Canaanite slave must be fed. It uses even the most lenient view about slaves to show how obvious the daughter's case would be.

phrases.english: If she is not fed, why does it need to be said?
Even according to the one who said
that a master can say to his slave:
'Work for me, and I will not feed you,'
that applies only to a Canaanite slave,
since 'with you' is not written about him.
But a Hebrew slave,
about whom 'with you' is written: no.
All the more so his daughter!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 12 as leaving the משנה with nothing to teach.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the משנה is about a daughter who is not fed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If even a Hebrew slave cannot be made to work without food, a daughter surely keeps her earnings when unfed, so the משנה's teaching would be pointless.

steps.title: The משנה is needed for the extra earnings
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר עולא explains that the משנה teaches about the surplus: what she earns beyond the cost of her food belongs to her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר עולא said: The משנה is needed only for the extra earnings (העדפה).
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר עולא answers the 'why say it' challenge by explaining that the משנה's hint ('after the father's death, to herself') is only about her surplus earnings. That keeps רב ששת's ruling in place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this reading, the משנה's hint that earnings after the father's death are 'hers' refers only to the extra beyond what covers her food. The brothers who feed her still get the basic earnings, as רב ששת ruled. Only the surplus belongs to her.

keyTerms.meaning: Surplus, earnings beyond what is needed for her food

phrases.english: Rabba bar Ulla said:
It is needed only for the extra earnings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'why say it' challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finding a new teaching in the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's hint seems to say that all of a fed daughter's earnings after the father's death are hers, against רב ששת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The hint only gives her the surplus. The brothers who feed her still take her basic earnings, so רב ששת stands.

steps.title: רבא: רב יוסף surely knew about the surplus
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects רבה בר עולא's answer. רב יוסף, a great scholar, would surely have known the surplus reading, so he would not have raised an objection that could be answered that easily.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Would a great man like רב יוסף not know that there is the surplus explanation, and still raise this objection?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on רבה בר עולא's answer and says it cannot be the real explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reasons from רב יוסף's greatness. If the surplus reading were enough to answer him, רב יוסף would have seen it himself. So his objection must have been about something the surplus reading does not solve.

phrases.english: Rava said:
A great man like Rav Yosef
wouldn't know that there is the surplus explanation,
and he raises an objection?

steps.triggerLanguage: גַּבְרָא רַבָּה כְּרַב יוֹסֵף לָא יָדַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבה בר עולא's surplus explanation as the answer to רב יוסף
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It is too obvious an answer for רב יוסף to have missed, so his objection must have meant something else.

steps.title: רבא's new explanation: the משנה's wording is strange
steps.stepSummary: רבא says רב יוסף's real difficulty came from the wording of the משנה itself. The משנה says 'even though she has not collected' about found items, but nobody 'collects' a found item from anyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: רב יוסף had a difficulty from the משנה itself. It says: 'her earnings and her found items, even though she has not collected them.' But from whom would she collect found items?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a new way to understand where רב יוסף's question came from. He points to a phrase in the משנה that does not make sense as it is written, which sets up his new reading in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Collecting' means getting payment from someone who owes you, like an employer who owes wages. A found item is already in your hands, so 'collecting' it makes no sense. That problem forces a different reading of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: itself (the משנה itself, not an inference from it)
her found item (a lost object she found)
she collected (received payment owed to her)

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: רַב יוֹסֵף מַתְנִיתִין גּוּפָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: Rav Yosef found the mishna itself difficult.
For it teaches: her earnings and her found items,
even though she has not collected them.
Her found items, from whom does she collect them?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: רַב יוֹסֵף מַתְנִיתִין גּוּפָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected explanation from step 15 with a new account of רב יוסף's reasoning.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plain wording of the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Collecting' cannot apply to a found item, so the משנה cannot mean what it seems to say.

steps.title: Her earnings are compared to her found items
steps.stepSummary: The משנה must mean 'her earnings are like her found items.' Found items go to the father while he lives and to her after he dies, so her earnings work the same way. This supports רב יוסף against רב ששת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the משנה must mean: her earnings are like her found items. Her found items go to the father while he is alive and to her after he dies. Her earnings also go to the father while he is alive and to her after he dies. We learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא solves the wording problem by reading the משנה as a comparison. That reading proves that after the father's death the daughter keeps her earnings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison covers all of her earnings, not just the extra beyond her food. So even when she is fed from the estate, her earnings are her own after her father dies, and that goes against רב ששת.

keyTerms.meaning: learn from this (a proof is established)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה is read as 'earnings are like found items,' so after the father dies the daughter keeps all her earnings, even while the estate feeds her.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that this is what it says:
Her earnings are like her found items:
phrases.notes: So the 'and' in the משנה is read as 'like.' That is the whole fix.

phrases.english: just as her found items in the father's lifetime go to the father,
and after the father's death go to herself,
so too her earnings as well:
in the father's lifetime, to the father,
after the father's death, to herself.
Learn from this.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו, הָכִי קָאָמַר: מַעֲשֵׂה יָדֶיהָ כִּמְצִיאָתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording difficulty of step 16 and turns it into a proof.
steps.raayaObject: That a daughter fed by the estate keeps her earnings after her father's death (against רב ששת)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה, read as comparing her earnings to her found items

steps.title: רב rules the same way: her earnings are her own
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings support from an אמורא: רב יהודה in the name of רב says that a daughter fed by the brothers keeps her earnings.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: a daughter who is fed by the brothers, her earnings belong to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds an explicit statement from רב that matches the conclusion of step 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 proved the rule from a reading of the משנה. Here an אמורא says it outright: even though the brothers feed her, they do not get her earnings.

keyTerms.meaning: it was also stated (support from an אמורא)

phrases.english: It was also stated:
Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
A daughter who is fed by the brothers,
her earnings belong to herself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר נָמֵי, אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the conclusion of step 17 with an explicit statement.
steps.raayaObject: A daughter fed by the brothers keeps her earnings
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב, as reported by רב יהודה

steps.title: רב כהנא's source from a verse
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא explains רב's ruling with a פסוק about slaves: you pass 'them' (slaves) to your sons, but not your daughters. So a father cannot leave his rights over his daughter to his son.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: What is the reason? It is written: 'And you shall bequeath them to your sons after you.' 'Them' you pass to your sons, but not your daughters to your sons. This teaches that a person does not pass his rights in his daughter on to his son.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא gives the source in the תורה for רב's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'them' limits what can be inherited to slaves. A father's rights over his daughter, such as her earnings, are personal to him and end when he dies, so the brothers do not inherit them.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a general principle: a father's rights over his daughter cannot be inherited by his sons.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said: What is the reason?
For it is written:
"And you shall bequeath them to your sons after you."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:46. The פסוק is talking about Canaanite slaves.

phrases.english: "Them to your sons",
and not your daughters to your sons.
This teaches that a person does not bequeath
his rights in his daughter to his son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural reason behind רב's ruling in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father's rights over his daughter are not inherited by his sons, so her earnings after his death are hers.

steps.title: רבה: the verse may refer only to seduction, fines, and injuries
steps.stepSummary: רבה challenges רב כהנא's source. The פסוק might be about payments for seduction, fines, and injuries, not about her earnings, and רב חנינא taught exactly that.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה objected: But say the פסוק is talking about payment for the seduction of the daughter, fines, and injuries. And so רב חנינא taught: the פסוק is talking about seduction of the daughter, fines, and injuries!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה attacks the proof from the פסוק by offering a narrower meaning, backed by a teaching of רב חנינא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק covers only money a father receives for harm done to his daughter, it proves nothing about her earnings. Then רב's ruling loses its source, because the brothers might still inherit the right to her earnings.

keyTerms.meaning: seduction (the payment owed to the father)
fines (paid when a girl is violated)

steps.confusionAlert: רבה is not saying the daughter's earnings go to the brothers. He is only saying this פסוק does not prove that they don't.

phrases.english: Rabba objected to it:
But say: about the seduction of the daughter,
phrases.notes: This is the payment the seducer gives the father. רבה is suggesting the פסוק talks only about these kinds of payments.

phrases.english: and fines and injuries, the verse is speaking.
And so Rav Chanina taught:
about the seduction of the daughter, fines, and injuries
the verse is speaking!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבָּה: וְאֵימָא בְּפִיתּוּי הַבַּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב כהנא's reading of the פסוק from step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's use of the פסוק as a source for the daughter's earnings
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק can be read narrowly as covering only seduction, fine, and injury payments, as רב חנינא taught, so it does not prove anything about earnings.

steps.title: Injuries are her own bodily pain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges including injuries on רב חנינא's list, because injury payments are for the girl's own bodily pain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Injuries? Those are pain to her own body!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions one item on רב חנינא's list from Step 20. Injury payments are for the girl's bodily pain, so how could they be something a father passes on to his son?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 said the פסוק covers payments for seduction, fines and injuries. Seduction payments and fines can be treated as the father's. Injuries are different, because the money pays for the girl's own suffering, so it seems it should belong to her. That makes injuries look out of place on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: Injuries, meaning payments for wounding someone
Pain of the body, suffering the person feels in her own body

phrases.english: Injuries? They are her bodily pain!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks one detail of רב חנינא's list, which רבה used in Step 20
steps.kashyaTarget: Including injuries on רב חנינא's list of payments the פסוק refers to
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Injury payments make up for the girl's own bodily suffering, so they should belong to her and not be something the father passes on

steps.title: רבי יוסי בר חנינא begins the answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces רבי יוסי בר חנינא, who will explain how injuries fit on the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said:
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. The גמרא is about to give רבי יוסי בר חנינא's answer to the question about injuries, and his words come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the name of the speaker appears here. His actual explanation of why injuries belong on the list continues right after this.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who will answer the question about injuries

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Ḥanina said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the question about injuries in Step 21
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explanation of the case, which continues after this line
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Injuries should not be on the list, because they are payment for the girl's own pain
steps.terutzMaskana: Not yet stated here; רבי יוסי בר חנינא's explanation follows
